oneliner.t: Two-term Republican congressman and former Navy SEAL (2001–2014) who co-founded Bottle Breacher. He unseated Democrat Tom O'Halleran 53.9%–46.1% in 2022 and beat Jonathan Nez 54.5%–45.5% in 2024. A Trump-endorsed House Freedom Caucus member who lives in Oro Valley, outside the district, he faces Nez again and Libertarian Curtis Goodwin.

upbringing.t: Born in Tucson and raised in Yuma, where his father was a pharmacist; he graduated from Cibola High School in 1998. He studied sociology at Arizona Western College and the University of Arizona without graduating and says he left college about a week after the Sept. 11 attacks to join the Navy. He served 2001–2014, including with SEAL Team 3. Wikipedia counts five deployments (three with the SEALs); a 2026 Arizona Mirror profile says six. With his wife, Jen, he co-founded Bottle Breacher in San Diego in 2012, pitched it on Shark Tank in 2014 and sold it in 2022. He has been a brand ambassador for Sig Sauer.

education.school: Arizona Western College; University of Arizona

career.role: U.S. Representative, AZ-2 (Homeland Security; Oversight and Government Reform)

platform.t: Calls himself an 'America First' candidate; opposes further Ukraine aid. His 2026 NDAA amendment to block Defense Department funding for Ukraine failed 76–350.
Rural Arizona: his revised 2026 site says he is 'committed to putting Rural Arizona first' and adds sections on protecting rural land and recovering from disasters such as the 2025 Globe flood.
Veterans: the 2026 site says veterans' care should take priority over 'fraud-ridden nongovernmental organizations.'

Water: sponsored the Yavapai Apache Water Rights Act (introduced December 2025; mirrored in the Senate by Kelly and Gallego). Accuses Gov. Hobbs of failing to protect Arizona's Colorado River allocation.
Judiciary: introduced articles of impeachment (Feb 2025) against U.S. District Judge Paul Engelmayer over his order blocking DOGE access to Treasury records.
Religion and law: founding member (Jan 2026) of the Sharia-Free America Caucus, which seeks to ban Sharia law. CAIR has designated the caucus an anti-Muslim hate group.
Abortion: called Roe v. Wade 'a mistake' and supported its reversal (2022). His 2026 About page dropped its earlier anti-abortion reference.
Elections (2022 platform): reinstate Election Day voting, end 'unregulated' mail-out ballots, stronger voter ID.

promises.t: Put rural Arizona first, including protecting rural land and disaster recovery.
Focus federal effort on veterans rather than 'fraud-ridden' NGOs.

claims.claim: Enlisted in the Navy shortly after 9/11, leaving college to do so.

said.where: campaign biography as reported by KJZZ; his account per Wikipedia

record.t: Navy service 2001–2014 is documented. The college exit (Arizona Western/University of Arizona, no degree) is consistent; the 'one week' timing is his own account.

said.where: campaign site (archived version), per Arizona Mirror

record.t: He co-founded Bottle Breacher in 2012 and sold it in 2022. His 2025 disclosure lists no current business, only interests in a court judgment enforcing repayment of the buyer's purchase loan.

claims.claim: Was the only candidate in the 2022 race endorsed by the National Border Patrol Council.

record.t: The union's 2022 endorsement list was not opened.
Ballotpedia separately lists him as a signer of the U.S. Term Limits pledge. U.S. Term Limits' own list was not opened.

claims.claim: Voted for the Fix Our Forests Act.

said.where: Facebook response to the Flagstaff town hall, per Navajo Times

record.t: Voted Yea on H.R. 471 passage, Roll Call 25, Jan 23, 2025 (279–141).

claims.claim: His office has returned more than $4 million to residents since January (tax refunds, veterans benefits, other federal claims).

record.t: Casework totals are self-reported; no independent record.

claims.claim: His third telephone town hall (Jul 22, 2025) drew more than 14,000 participants.
The U.S. has given Israel just over $150 billion since its founding.

record.t: Wikipedia, citing the Congressional Research Service: $150 billion in bilateral assistance, not adjusted for inflation, through February 2022.

claims.claim: The U.S. has sent over $135 billion to Ukraine since the conflict began.

record.t: No source on cumulative Ukraine aid as of October 2023 was opened.

claims.claim: The Biden administration released $6 billion to Iran on Sept. 11, 2023, without accountability.

record.t: The Wikipedia page on the 2023 prisoner exchange could not be fetched, so the transfer's terms (Iranian funds moved to restricted humanitarian accounts) were not checked here.

said.t: His campaign site, archived Jul 19, 2026, opposed 'funding forever wars'; early in the Iran war he said he worried it could become a long, costly 'forever war.'

did.t: Voted against a June 2026 war-powers resolution that would have limited the Iran war absent congressional authorization (roll call in the key-votes file). By September 2026 his site no longer contained the forever-wars language. His campaign did not respond to questions.

said.t: Backed continued U.S. support for Israel and said Israel aid should be judged on its own merits, not bundled with Ukraine aid.

did.t: Voted Nay on the stand-alone Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act (H.R. 8034), which passed 366–58. His stated reason for that vote was not found in the sources opened.

said.t: His campaign site (until summer 2026) promised to 'rein in reckless spending'; that fiscal section was later deleted.

did.t: Voted against the 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act (one of 71 Republicans), but voted for the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut SNAP and Medicaid and which the Arizona Mirror, citing an estimate, says adds $4.7 trillion to the debt.

promises_prev.promise: Border security: return to 'President Trump's border policies' (2022 campaign).

evidence.t: Voted for the Laken Riley Act (S. 5) on Jan 22, 2025; it passed the House 263–156. He also voted for H.R. 2 (2023); that roll call is in the key-votes file.

complicating.t: The Laken Riley Act covers only a narrow part of the 2022 pledge. Broader 2025 border-policy changes, and any role he played in them, were not documented in the sources opened. Ballotpedia lists H.R. 2 (Secure the Border Act of 2023) among his key votes; its later fate was not checked here.

promises_prev_note: Other 2022 promises (U.S. Term Limits pledge, ending 'unregulated' mail ballots, banning federal gain-of-function funding) were not checked against his sponsorships; they are left out rather than given a status.

entries.t: Told Steve Bannon on May 9 that Ukraine aid money should go to stopping illegal immigration in Arizona.
Op-ed cites Ukraine's corruption ranking and warns deeper involvement risks a longer war and nuclear escalation.
Offered an NDAA amendment to block DoD funding to Ukraine; it failed 76–350.
Opposed Kevin McCarthy on every speaker ballot, voting 'present' on the 15th; in October he was one of eight Republicans who voted to remove McCarthy.
Claimed the Butler gunman did not act alone and that the Florida gunman was an 'asset' of a foreign adversary.

statements.t: After the Hamas attack, said Israel is entitled to defend itself with overwhelming force, that there is no moral equivalence, and that 'America must stand with Israel.' He also blamed the Biden administration's release of Iranian funds.
Newsweek op-ed opposing Biden's request to bundle $14.3B for Israel with $61.4B for Ukraine; said Israel aid should stand on its own merits and border security should come first.
Said he was worried the U.S.–Israeli attack on Iran could become another long Middle East 'forever war.'
Said he was 'really, really hopeful' the Iran conflict would not involve U.S. ground troops.

democracy.t: Promoted claims of 'massive amounts of fraud' in the 2020 presidential election, called on the Arizona Legislature to decertify Biden's win in the state, and urged the state attorney general to open a criminal investigation (date not given in the source; before he took office).
KJZZ reported that, along with Trump, he continued to claim significant fraud in the 2020 election, and noted there is no evidence for the claims.
